1Platform Navigation

Once logged in, open your course. The course has these main sections:

  • Announcements
  • Lessons
  • Attendance
  • Quizzes
  • Homework
  • Recordings
  • Group Chat

1.1 Announcements

Use this section for important notices, exam information, public holidays, and schedule changes.

Students also receive an email notification for each announcement.

1.2 Lessons

This section holds all teaching content:

  • The course-materials download page (download PDF)
  • Teaching slides
  • Any supplementary materials teachers upload

Students can download materials for review. To add material, click the + button next to Course Materials at the top of the page. Available file types are h5p, pdf, audio, text, and video.

Note

The H5P version of materials is updated by the school.

1.3 Attendance

Mandatory — immigration record

Immigration requires a study record for every student. If attendance is missing, a student's French result can't be documented, even after they pass. Update it on time. Classes with no attendance record also forfeit the attendance bonus.

This section records both student and teacher attendance.

  • The attendance page becomes active after the class start time.
  • Changes can be made within 24 hours.
  • Please update attendance promptly.

1.4 Quizzes — finish grading within 3 working days

All exams and quiz grading happen in this section.

Students can

  • Access the exam within the scheduled time
  • Click START QUIZ to open the exam page
  • Complete the quiz within the time limit
  • Submit answers before the deadline

Students are generally allowed two attempts, in case of unexpected system issues. If a student hits a technical problem, they should tell the teacher immediately.

Teachers can

  • Monitor exam attempts
  • Review submissions (GRADE QUIZ)
  • Manually grade subjective questions (GRADE QUIZ)
  • Provide feedback (GRADE QUIZ)

To grade a submission, open the student's attempt and click Attempt to correct the exam. After grading, students see their results, the reference answers, and teacher feedback for the writing and speaking parts (once you click Submit feedback).

Deadline

Complete grading within three working days — including reviewing submissions, manually grading subjective questions, and providing feedback.

1.5 Homework — system update in progress; auto-grading

This section includes supplementary assignments, automatic grading for multiple-choice questions, and reference answers for written questions.

Teacher steps

  1. Click on each student's submission
  2. Select Grade homework
  3. Submit feedback

Students will then see their results, the correct answers, and teacher comments.

1.6 Recordings

Zoom recordings are automatically saved to the Recordings section if you joined every session.

  • Recordings are available for 7 days.
  • Students may use them for review and revision.

1.7 Group Chat

Each course has a class discussion group (Discussions) where teachers and students can message each other.

1.8 H5P question types

Course materials use interactive H5P slides (an interactive PPT). On the slide bar, a circle marker (O) means that slide has an interactive practice question.

Order — drag the numbers

Drag each number into the correct square, then click Check.

Single-choice

One correct answer. No question mark means there is only one question. For listening exercises, a ? button in the corner shows the full question list, so students can read ahead before the audio plays.

Side-by-side layout

A split-column layout: primary questions on one side, contextual options or descriptions on the other.

Fill in the blanks

Type the answer in each box, then click Check. Correct entries turn green; wrong entries turn red.

Fill-in-the-blank scoring — avoid errors

Punctuation: if a period (.) or question mark (?) is already built into the sentence outside the blank, do not retype it inside the answer box — the extra punctuation marks the answer wrong.

Apostrophes: the curved French apostrophe (’) and the straight typewriter apostrophe (') may be treated as different characters. Match the expected character to prevent grading discrepancies.

Matching / drag to target

Drag each phrase or label to the correct square or target.

Multiple-choice

A square box means two or more answers; a circle means a single answer.

Listening transcript

Click the ? on the audio player (or beside a multiple-choice question) to open the listening transcript. On some slides the transcript is on the next page.

2Zoom Guide

Before you start

Install the Zoom desktop application on your device. The web version does not always have the same functions.

2.1 Recording

  • Zoom recording starts automatically when you open it.
  • Recordings are uploaded to the platform's Recordings section.
  • Recordings stay available for 7 days.

To open Zoom: in Lessons, click Join Live Session → Join Zoom, then Open zoom.us / Join from the Zoom Workplace app. If the app doesn't open, download and install it, then click Join again.

2.2 Screen sharing

Always check “Share Sound”

Without it, students will not hear audio from videos, listening exercises, recordings, or your shared screen.

When you share, pick the screen or window, then tick Share sound (and Optimize for video sharing for videos) before clicking Share.

2.3 Annotating the screen

While sharing, use the annotation toolbar to write on the screen. Tools include text, brush, mark/highlight, and eraser, plus undo/redo and the trash icon to clear everything.

2.4 Host role & waiting room

You need the host role to run the oral exam and to manage the waiting room.

Host code

The host code is sent to teachers before the test. For oral exams, the same code unlocks the courseware — see Section 3.

Claim the host role

  1. Click Participants in the Zoom toolbar.
  2. At the bottom, open More (Plus) and choose Claim host / Revendiquer le rôle d'hôte.
  3. Enter the host key and click Revendiquer.

Activate the waiting room

  1. Open Participants → More (Plus).
  2. Choose Activate waiting room / Activer la salle d'attente.

Move a student to the waiting room

  1. Hover the student, then click More (Plus).
  2. Choose Put in waiting room / Mettre en salle d'attente.

Admit a student back

Click Admit / Admettre next to the student's name in the waiting room.

3Oral Exam Procedure

The same procedure applies to every level. Screenshots in the source use A1 Mid as an example.

One code — Zoom host role + oral courseware

927145

3.1 Before exam day — preview the questions

The oral exam questions live inside the platform courseware and are ready in your exam-day class session. Unlock them with code 927145. You can also preview the listening / reading / writing parts.

The preview link opens the quiz preview on the MLI platform (login required). The real exam is taken online by the students. Use the CO · CE · EE tabs and full-screen toggle to move through the parts.

3.2 On exam day — Zoom & waiting room (1-on-1)

  1. Claim the host role with host key 927145.
  2. Turn on the Waiting Room.
  3. Admit one student at a time; keep the others in the waiting room.
  4. When a student is finished, move them out and admit the next one.

The exact Zoom steps (also in Section 2.4):

3.3 Run & grade with the courseware

  • Unlock with 927145 and share your screen.
  • Étudiant (Student) mode — present each task: draw the lottery, start the timer.
  • Examinateur (Examiner) mode — fill the rubric, then Export PDF or record the EO score (see grading below).
Do not share the code with students

Code 927145 is for teachers only.

3.4 Oral question sets

The oral question banks live in the courseware and open with code 927145. Use the set that matches the class and whether it is the mid or the final exam.

4Grading

You mainly handle EE (writing) and EO (oral). The written exam (CO · CE · EE) is on the platform: Course Homepage → Quiz (opens only at class time).

Mandatory — immigration record

Grades and transcripts are part of each student's official study record for immigration. A missing transcript means a passed exam can't be proven — grade every student on time.

SkillWhat you do
CO — ListeningMultiple-choice, graded automatically. Nothing to do.
CE — ReadingMultiple-choice, graded automatically. Nothing to do.
EE — WritingGrade manually on the platform (GRADE QUIZ): score + feedback.
EO — OralRecord your rubric score / feedback in the blank EO field (after the writing section).
Deadline

Finish grading within 3 working days.

Writing (EE) rubrics

Two rubrics are used, depending on the exam. In both, you enter points in the yellow columns and the score is calculated for you.

RubricUsed forHow it scores
MLI rubricA1, A2, Phase 1, Phase 2 (mid)Content /8 · Grammar /7 · Spelling /5 · Word count /5 = /25
TCF rubricPhase 2 Final, CLB5, CLB6, CLB74 criteria × /5 (Instruction · Coherence · Vocabulary · Grammar & spelling) = /20 → auto NCLC

MLI rubric — criteria (A1, A2, Phase 1, Phase 2 mid)

CriterionPoints
1. Topic / content (letter format, describes new city & life)/8
2. Grammar (A1–A2 structures)/7
3. Spelling/5
4. Word count (≥50 words = 5; scales down to 0 under 10)/5
Total/25

TCF rubric — criteria (Phase 2 Final, CLB5, CLB6, CLB7)

Three tasks: 1 — short informal message (~60–120 words); 2 — formal message / letter / article (~120–150); 3 — synthesis of two documents + argued opinion (~120–180). The /20 covers the whole production.

CriterionPoints
1. Respect of the instruction & the three tasks/5
2. Coherence & cohesion/5
3. Vocabulary / lexis/5
4. Morphosyntax & spelling/5
Total/20 → NCLC
Give one direct score

The official TCF way tags each task with a CEFR level (A1 / A2 / B1 / B2). MLI needs a single number instead: on the TCF rubric, score the four criteria 0–5 for the production as a whole to get a mark out of 20 — the sheet converts it to NCLC automatically. Enter that score on the platform.

NCLC score bands (TCF Canada)

NCLCSpeaking (EO)Listening (CO)Reading (CE)Writing (EE)
10+16–20549–699549–69916–20
914–15523–548524–54814–15
812–13503–522499–52312–13
710–11458–502453–49810–11

56369–397375–4056
44–5331–368342–3744–5

Speaking (EO) uses the same 0–20 bands as Writing. Rubric files open alongside this handbook.

Revising a graded answer

If an answer was already graded but is incorrect, or there is a capitalization issue:

  1. Retract feedback.
  2. Click the answer states to correct them.

Answer-state colours: Green = correct · Red = wrong · Transparent background = unselected / default.

5Exam Structure

Class typeStages
Phase classesPhase 1 → Phase 2 → Phase 3
CLB classesCLB4 A0+A1 → CLB4 A2 → CLB5 → CLB6 → CLB7
Which stage sits which exam
  • Débutant — Phase class: Phase 1 · CLB class: CLB4 A0+A1
  • Pré-intermédiaire — Phase class: Phase 2 · CLB class: CLB4 A2
  • Intermédiaire — Phase class: Phase 3 · CLB class: CLB6 & CLB7 (full TCF)
  • CLB5 now takes the Phase 2 Final exam — a reduced TCF format (details below).

CLB5, CLB6 and CLB7 all use TCF questions, so for those classes teachers do not need to preview the written parts (CO · CE auto-grade and EE uses the TCF rubric) — only the oral (EO) teacher prepares, using the TCF EO set for the level (see Oral question sets).

5.1 Phase 1 · CLB4 A0+A1 (3 hours)

TimeContent
Hour 1Written exam (60 min) — Listening + Reading + Writing
Hour 2Oral test (1-on-1, 8–10 min per student)
Hour 3Continue orals if needed / feedback

5.2 Phase 2 · CLB4 A2 (3 hours)

TimeContent
0h – 2hWritten exam (120 min) — Listening + Reading + Writing
After 1h30Oral can begin if the group has more than 6 students
2h – 3hContinue orals / feedback
Reminder

Class cannot end before the scheduled time.

5.3 Phase 3 — TCF-style (CLB5 · CLB6 · CLB7)

Phase 3 exams follow a TCF-style format. Each skill has an independent exam paper.

Listening

Audio is played once only — the same as the official TCF exam.

Skill breakdown

SkillCLB5 — Phase 2 FinalCLB6 / CLB7
ListeningQ1–20 only39 questions (full TCF)
ReadingQ1–20 only39 questions (full TCF)
WritingTask 1 & 2 onlyTask 1, 2 & 3
SpeakingTask 1 & 2 onlyTask 1, 2 & 3
ScheduleSame day — 1 teacher covers all sections; 2 teachers split by section (in parallel)Split over 2 days

CLB5 now takes the same exam as the Phase 2 Final — the reduced format above (Q1–20; Tasks 1 & 2; same day), which eases students into the full TCF.

CLB5 — arrangement

It depends on the teaching staff. With one teacher, the whole exam can be run and graded in a single day. With two teachers, split the exam by section — each teacher runs and grades their own part, and the sections can go in parallel on the same day.

CLB6 / CLB7 — arrangement

  • The exam is split over 2 days.
  • Format closely follows the full TCF exam.
  • The Day 1 / Day 2 schedule is confirmed by the academic team.
CLB6 / CLB7 — nothing extra to prepare

All four skills come straight from the TCF bank. CO / CE are auto-graded and EE uses the TCF rubric, so there is nothing special for teachers to prepare — only the oral (EO) teacher prepares, using the TCF EO set for the level (see Oral question sets).

6TCF Canada Training Tools · 2026

These online tools help students prepare for the TCF Canada. They cover all four skills — listening, reading, written expression, and oral expression — and support independent work with automatic correction and PDF export to make your follow-up easier. Everything runs in the browser, with no installation.

Internal use — do not share links

These four practice tools cover all four skills and are updated continuously (the current month is added by the end of the month). They are for teacher use; access is provided separately by the school — please don't pass the tool links to students. A preview of each tool is shown below.

6.1 Listening & Reading — 40 series per skill

Students train on 40 complete series per skill (individual-series mode). At the end of each series the score is calculated automatically, the estimated NCLC level is shown, and the list of wrong questions can be exported as a PDF — a strong starting point for remediation in class.

New — de-duplicated & reclassified banks

The questions from the 40 series are now grouped, de-duplicated, and reorganized: reading is classified by difficulty (1–4, 5–10, 11–19, 20–29, 30–35, 36–39) and listening by category. Each question appears only once, which allows targeted practice on weak points.

Targeted-practice mode has no NCLC scoring. For the score and the error export, use individual-series mode.

6.2 Written expression (EE) — 2026 edition

Subject bank, updated continuously — the current month's real subjects are added by the end of each month. The subjects that actually appeared are classified by theme and browsable by month, with the most frequent subjects flagged — ideal for steering students toward priority topics.

Mock-exam mode (Épreuve blanche)

A full subject (Task 1 + Task 2 + Task 3) is drawn at random from subjects that appeared together. The page reproduces real exam conditions:

  • A 60-minute timer at the top of the page
  • An integrated French keyboard — accents and special characters (é è ê à ç…) available in one click
  • A word counter per task, with a reminder of the expected ranges
  • PDF export of the copy at the end, to hand to the teacher for correction

6.3 Oral expression (EO) — 2026 edition

Subject bank, updated continuously — the current month's real subjects are added by the end of each month. The oral subjects (Task 2 — guided interaction; Task 3 — sustained monologue) are classified by theme and by month, with recurring subjects flagged.

Task 3 subjects can be heard in a synthesized voice — as close as possible to the real exam, where the instruction is heard aloud. Task 2 is presented in writing.

6.4 Summary

SkillWhat the student gets
ListeningIndividual series: 40 series · auto score · NCLC · PDF export of errorsDe-duplicated bank: targeted practice by category (no scoring)
ReadingIndividual series: 40 series · auto score · NCLC · PDF export of errorsDe-duplicated bank: targeted practice by level (no scoring)
WritingSubject bank by theme / month (updated monthly) · 1-hour mock exam: timer, French keyboard, word counter, PDF export
SpeakingSubject bank by theme / month (updated monthly) · Tasks 2 & 3 · Task 3 in synthesized voice

Feel free to share these tools with your students, and to send feedback so we can keep improving them.
